sources.name: USDA FoodData Central records queried for illustrative food-composition anchors

records.description: Tomatoes, red, ripe, raw, year round average
Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

sources.relevance: Only illustrative nutrient centers; these data have no packaging recommendation labels and do not validate the generated target.
sources.limitations: Four specific database records are not population ranges. FDC does not provide pH, respiration, package properties or a food-to-material recommendation target. The biscuit and frozen-vegetable profiles use declared demonstration centers, not values attributed to these four records.

sources.name: Tomato Produce Fact Sheet
sources.source: UC Davis Postharvest Research and Extension Center
sources.license: Educational use restrictions stated by UC Davis; source is linked and paraphrased, not redistributed
sources.relevance: Supports the two tomato respiration anchors and the relationship between respiration, temperature, gas exchange and produce handling.
sources.limitations: Rates vary by maturity and conditions. They are not packaging labels or package-specific respiration experiments.

sources.name: Food packaging permeability and composition dataset dedicated to text-mining
sources.source: Data in Brief / TRANSMAT Gold Standard Dataverse
sources.license: Article reports open access under CC BY 4.0; confirm the Dataverse file-level terms before redistributing files
sources.rows: The landing article describes annotations from 50 scientific articles; a dataset-row total is not stated on the inspected landing page.
sources.files: Four annotation files are described: three annotator files and one consensus Gold Standard.
sources.relevance: Material/permeability literature data; not a dataset of food properties, storage conditions and recommended-material labels.
sources.limitations: Built for text mining / entity and relation extraction. It cannot directly train the requested supervised recommendation target. Not used as training data.

sources.name: Mapping gas permeability of sustainable packaging materials to link food barrier needs by clustering algorithms
sources.source: npj Science of Food article and Food-Pack-Mapper repository
sources.license: Paper is open access; repository/data-package license was not confirmed during this inspection
sources.relevance: Useful published material-permeability observations across packaging literature.
sources.limitations: Material-property clustering, not observed food + route → selected packaging labels. Conditions are missing for a material subset. Not used as recommendation training data; no files copied.

sources.name: Data for: Predicting shelf life gain of fresh produce in Modified Atmosphere Packaging
sources.source: Mendeley Data, Valérie Guillard et al.
sources.rows: The inspected landing page does not state a row count.
sources.columns: The inspected landing page does not enumerate a table schema; it describes supplementary material for a basic MAP design model.
sources.limitations: Does not expose a complete, general food-property + storage + recommended-material classification table on the landing page. Not used as training data.

sources.name: R3PACK WP4 Dataset T4.5 - Shelf-life simulation results for snack products
sources.license: No license value was shown in the inspected record; no redistribution assumed
sources.files: One XLSX workbook (SimulationResults_Snacks.xlsx; 163.2 kB on the record page)
sources.rows: The record page does not state workbook row counts.
sources.columns: Record description says an Overview sheet includes simulation conditions/package properties and other tabs contain simulation outputs; exact schemas were not available on the inspected landing page.
sources.relevance: Promising snack-package simulation results with packaging and storage conditions.
sources.limitations: Model-simulation outputs for snacks, not experimental ground-truth material recommendations across foods. No verified material-class target. Not used as training data.

sources.name: Modelling approaches for designing and evaluating the performance of modified atmosphere packaging (MAP) systems for fresh produce: A review
sources.relevance: Documents the coupled role of produce physiology/respiration, gas permeability and storage conditions in MAP design.
sources.limitations: A review of design approaches; not a label table for the prototype classifier.

sources.name: Modified Atmosphere Packaging Technology of Fresh and Fresh-cut Produce and the Microbial Consequences—A Review
sources.source: International Journal of Food Microbiology review
sources.relevance: Explains that produce respiration, film permeability, temperature, package area/thickness and headspace jointly determine MAP; cautions about unsafe atmospheres.
sources.limitations: No general recommendation model labels; package design remains commodity- and condition-specific.

sources.name: Cereal and Confectionary Packaging: Background, Application and Shelf-Life Extension
sources.relevance: Discusses oxygen and water-vapor barriers for cereals/confectionery and the oxidation/crispness concerns for fried, oil-rich snacks.
sources.limitations: Qualitative design context; it does not supply a universally valid material property for an unspecified laminate.

sources.name: A Meta-study of the Permeance of Perforated Packaging Films to Oxygen and Carbon Dioxide
sources.relevance: Supports treating perforation-dependent gas permeance separately from an unperforated base-film OTR.
sources.limitations: Does not set a universal perforation design for the prototype foods.

sources.name: Banana (Cavendish) Postharvest Produce Fact Sheet
sources.source: UC Davis Postharvest Research and Extension Center
sources.license: Educational use restrictions; linked and paraphrased, not redistributed
sources.relevance: Supports the illustrative banana profile, two respiration anchors and the banana-specific storage/transport warning.
sources.limitations: The fact sheet is about Cavendish bananas and dates to 1996. Respiration varies with maturity and condition. It does not label a preferred carton or validate this model.

sources.name: Small-Scale Postharvest Handling Practices, Chapter 7: Packing containers
sources.source: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.license: FAO publication; cited and paraphrased, not redistributed
fields_used: banana hands packed in cardboard containers lined with polyethylene
packing arrangement to reduce transport damage
sources.relevance: Directly documents a banana carton/liner format and ventilation guidance used to define the curated target class.
sources.limitations: The illustrated guidance does not specify modern carton grade, liner gauge/perforation, dimensions, compression values or applicability to every cultivar and market. It does not establish a comparative optimum.

sources.name: FoodOn food product terminology
sources.relevance: Bundled English food-product labels and synonyms are used by the backend to distinguish recognized unseen foods from invalid commodity strings.
sources.limitations: Vocabulary only; it supplies no nutritional measurements, packaging labels, compatibility decisions or model training examples.
